reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the artifacts are internally consistent: the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment was emitted, which is what a compliant finding should look like.

The cited text supports compliance on the rule's material terms: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional right to give 'written notice of its election to terminate' with no cause, consent, or exit fee requirement, and service continues only to the last day of the following month (~30-60 days' effective notice), i.e., at or within the preferred/fallback notice window.

Vendor-side risk is correctly analysed: Section 13 sets a 1-year term with 1-year renewals and TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off (partial termination of Sections 2-3) is cause-based, so neither walk-away trigger (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term; Vendor convenience on <90 days) is engaged.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is adequately explained as a phrasing artefact - the right is drafted obliquely as TrueLink's continuing obligation up to the Client-elected termination date rather than as express 'terminate for convenience' wording - so the regex miss is evidence of a variant, not a substantive gap.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position (no express pro-rata refund, monthly arrears billing making prepayment largely moot, 30-day mutual non-renewal notice) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements, and tightening the mutual non-renewal notice would cut against our own flexibility.

The unresolved 'Subject to Section 4' cross-reference (potential minimum-monthly-fee tail) is flagged as an open item for confirmation rather than asserted as a breach, which is an appropriate hedge and does not undermine the compliant classification on the reviewed text.
